findings.description: The user_data script embeds plaintext AWS access key ID (AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMAAA) and secret access key (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) exported as environment variables. These credentials are written to the instance and exposed to anyone with access to the instance, console output, or the Terraform state, enabling unauthorized access to the AWS account.

The EBS volume is created without encryption enabled (the encrypted argument is absent/commented out). Any data stored on the attached volume, including the web host's application data, is stored in plaintext at rest, exposing it if the underlying storage is compromised or the volume is moved.

The EBS snapshot is taken of an unencrypted volume and does not specify encryption, so the snapshot and any cross-region or cross-account copy of it will be unencrypted at rest. Data from the volume is exposed in the snapshot in plaintext.

Ingress rule allows SSH (port 22/tcp) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing the web host to any host on the internet. This dramatically expands the attack surface for brute-force and credential-stuffing attacks against the instance over SSH.

Ingress rule allows HTTP (port 80/tcp) from 0.0.0.0/0 with no network boundary restriction. While port 80 is the intended web service port, combined with the public IP assignment this exposes the host to the entire internet without restricting source networks.

map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, so instances launched in this subnet automatically receive a public IP. Combined with the unrestricted SSH ingress in the attached security group, this exposes the instance directly to the internet.

map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, so any instance launched in this subnet automatically receives a public IP, making it directly reachable from the internet rather than via a controlled network boundary.
The S3 bucket used to store VPC flow logs does not enable server-side encryption. VPC flow log records, which can contain sensitive metadata about network traffic, are stored in plaintext in S3.
